relevance_reason: Reports a cohort of 15 LGMDR21 patients from 9 families with biallelic POGLUT1 variants, with clinical, imaging, pathology and functional characterization.

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) reported 15 patients from 9 unrelated families with LGMDR21 from Spain, Bulgaria, Italy, Germany, USA, Iran and the United Arab Emirates. Four of the families were consanguineous. Onset was congenital in 1 patient, infantile (before age 3 years) in 2, and adult in 12. Weakness was proximal, predominated in the lower limbs and progressed slowly. Seven patients with onset in their teens needed a wheelchair between the third and fifth decades. Eleven patients had mild to moderate scapular winging.
quotes: We identified one patient with a congenital presentation, two patients with infantile onset before 3 years of age, and 12 patients with adult onset (58.3% in 2nd decade, 25% in 3rd decade, and 16.6% in 4th-5th decade).

The weakness showed a proximal distribution, with a clear predominance in the lower limbs and slow progression. Seven patients (46.6%) with onset in their teens, were confined to wheelchair between the 3th and 5th decade. Mild to moderate scapular winging was present in 11 of the 15 patients.
Consanguinity was recognized in four of the nine families.

phenotypes.text: proximal lower limb predominant muscle weakness

findings.population: Spain, Bulgaria, Italy, Germany, USA, Iran, United Arab Emirates

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) found mild to severe respiratory involvement in 6 patients from their mid-forties onward, whatever the age at onset. Two of these patients used ventilatory support at night. There were no significant bulbar, cardiac or other systemic manifestations. Serum CK was normal in most patients, and the authors noted this as a diagnostic hint that distinguishes LGMDR21 from most other recessive LGMDs.
quotes: Mild to severe respiratory involvement was present in six patients (only two with ventilatory support at night) from the mid-forties onwards, regardless of the age at onset. No significant bulbar, cardiac or other systemic manifestations were detected.
The level of serum CK was normal, except for four patients who showed mild elevation ranging from x2 to x6 the normal level.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

phenotypes.text: normal serum CK in most patients

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) described a 24-year-old male with congenital onset (family 2, patient II.1). He presented with hypotonia, then developed proximal lower limb weakness after learning to walk. Later he developed weakness, wasting and contractures in the upper limbs, mild facial weakness, ptosis, nasal voice, elbow contractures, myopathic facies and an arched palate, and he used a wheelchair from age 22. Progression was faster and more severe than in the adult-onset cases.
quotes: The presenting symptom in the congenital case was hypotonia with lower limb proximal weakness after gait acquisition, and further progression with mild weakness, wasting and contractures of the upper limbs (Fig. 1b). This patient with congenital presentation showed mild facial weakness, ptosis, and nasal voice.
2/ II.1 | p.D233E/ p.R279Q | 1st | 24/M | Congenital onset | 2 | 5 | 3–4 | 5 | N | Yes | >80 | Yes/22 | Elbow contractureMyopathic faciesArched palate
The congenital case presented with a similar distribution of muscle weakness with faster and more severe progression.

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) described 2 patients with infantile onset. The first, a 46-year-old man homozygous for I129T (family 3), used a wheelchair from age 33 and had ankle contracture, calf hypertrophy, scoliosis and hyperlordosis. The second, a 19-year-old man homozygous for R183W (family 9), used a wheelchair from age 13 and had nystagmus and retinitis pigmentosa.

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) reviewed lower limb muscle MRI or CT in 11 of the 15 patients, and all 11 showed an 'inside-to-outside' pattern of fatty degeneration. The inner segments of the vastus lateralis, vastus medialis and vastus intermedius, the posterior thigh compartment and the gastrocnemius were affected first. Lower leg muscles were better preserved than thigh muscles. The pattern was clearest early in the disease but could still be seen in the vastus lateralis at end stage.
quotes: Muscle imaging studies of the lower limbs were available from 11 of 15 patients. The muscle MRI or CT depicted a so called “from inside-to-outside” pattern of fatty degeneration in all the patients (Fig. 2).

This special pattern of partial degeneration of the muscles, starting in the inner segments, specifically involved the vastus lateralis, medialis and intermedius, the posterior thigh compartment and the gastrocnemius muscles.
The lower leg muscles were better preserved than thigh muscles, even when the thigh showed an advanced degeneration

phenotypes.text: inside-to-outside fatty degeneration of thigh muscles on MRI

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) examined muscle biopsies from 9 patients belonging to 6 families. Vastus lateralis biopsies were dystrophic. Biceps brachii biopsies showed mild myopathic features, and some had lobulated fibers. Immunostaining showed reduced glycosylated alpha-dystroglycan at the sarcolemma in all biopsies, while staining for the alpha-dystroglycan core was normal. Western blots confirmed the hypoglycosylation and showed reduced laminin binding.
quotes: We studied the muscle biopsy from nine of the 15 patients (belonging to six of the nine families).

Immunofluorescence staining with an antibody against glycosylated α-dystroglycan revealed a reduction of the glycosylated form of α-dystroglycan at the sarcolemma in all muscle biopsies, in contrast to the normal staining by antibodies against the α-dystroglycan core (Fig. 3a).

Western blots showed a reduction in α-dystroglycan glycosylation and small decrease in the molecular weight of glycosylated α-dystroglycan in skeletal muscle, together with a diminished laminin-binding activity in the ligand overlay assay

findings.statement: In patient muscle, Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) found reduced NOTCH1 intracellular domain (NICD) and a significantly reduced number of PAX7-positive satellite cells (5 patients vs 5 controls). There were no or very few eMHC-positive regenerating fibers, whereas disease controls had many. The authors suggested that reduced Notch1 signaling disturbs satellite cell biology and causes the dystrophy. They proposed that alpha-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation contributes as a secondary defect.
quotes: Western blots also demonstrated that the NOTCH1-intracellular-domain (NICD) level in skeletal muscle was decreased in patients compared to controls (Fig. 4a)
we found a reduced number of PAX7+ cells in the muscle of patients (Fig. 4b, c).

We found no staining of eMHC or a few scattered, eMHC+ myofibers in patients with POGLUT1 mutations, in contrast to disease controls (including muscle dystrophies and congenital myopathies), which showed many eMHC+ myofibers (Fig. 4d).

findings.statement: Using next-generation sequencing (gene panels or whole-exome sequencing) with Sanger confirmation, Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) identified 9 missense variants and 1 nonsense variant in POGLUT1, homozygous or compound heterozygous, in 15 patients from 9 families with LGMDR21. In every family the variants segregated with disease, and no asymptomatic carriers were found. The novel variants were absent from ExAC or seen in the heterozygous state in at most 2 of more than 60,000 non-Finnish European controls.
quotes: Sequencing data analysis identified nine missense and one nonsense recessive variants (homozygous or compound heterozygous) in the POGLUT1 gene, in 15 patients from nine independent families from seven different countries
Study of affected and unaffected relatives confirmed correct segregation of the disease with the homozygous or compound heterozygous state for the POGLUT1 variants.

All variants were either absent (p.I129T, p.W308L and p.W184*) or found in heterozygous state in one (p.R98W and p.C102F) or two individuals (p.Y156N and p.Y57C) out of >60,000 healthy European (Non-Finnish) controls

findings.statement: In the male patient with congenital-onset disease (family 2, II.1), Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) identified POGLUT1 variants D233E and R279Q, both found by NGS panel sequencing. The clinical table and the myoblast experiments describe him as compound heterozygous (p.D233E/p.R279Q). R279Q had previously been reported in the heterozygous state in a patient with Dowling-Degos disease. Based on the protein structure, R279Q was predicted to interfere with donor substrate binding. The patient's myoblasts proliferated less and differentiated faster than controls.
quotes: primary myoblasts from the congenital case carrying the compound heterozygous mutations p.D233E/ p.R279Q were cultured and compared to healthy controls (Fig. 7).
The variant p.R279Q (previously described in a Dowling-Degos disease [DDD] patient as a heterozygous mutation) was identified as homozygous in patient II.1 from Family 2.
R279Q is predicted to interfere with donor binding in human POGLUT1

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) identified a homozygous POGLUT1 missense variant, I129T, in a man with infantile-onset LGMDR21 (family 3). The variant was absent from ExAC. In HEK293T cells the mutant protein was secreted poorly and was not detected in cell lysates, suggesting severe destabilization. It did not rescue Notch1 EGF1-18 secretion in POGLUT1-knockout cells. In Drosophila it was expressed normally but only partially rescued myogenesis.
quotes: The homozygous missense variants p.I129T, p.R98W, p.Y57C, p.W308L, p.C102F (novel variants), and p.R183W (previously described as a DDD mutation) were identified in patients from Families 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9 respectively.
The p.I129T mutant was not detected in cell lysates either, suggesting it causes a more severe destabilization of the protein, at least in HEK293T cells.

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) identified a homozygous POGLUT1 missense variant, R98W, in 3 sisters with adult-onset LGMDR21 (family 4). The variant was seen in the heterozygous state in 1 ExAC control. In HEK293T cells secretion of the mutant protein was much reduced, and the mutant gave little or no rescue of Notch1 EGF1-18 secretion in POGLUT1-knockout cells. Its expression was also reduced in Drosophila.
quotes: 4/ II.1 | p.R98W/ p.R98W | 5th | 52/F | LGMD- adult onset | 4- | 5 | 4 | 5 | N | Yes | 72 | No |
These results suggest that the p.R98W, p.C102F, p.I129T, and p.W308L mutants of POGLUT1 have little or no ability to rescue secretion of Notch1 EGF1–18-MycHis in these assays.

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) identified a homozygous POGLUT1 missense variant, Y57C, in a woman with adult-onset LGMDR21 (family 5). The mutant protein was secreted normally but had much lower in vitro O-glucosyltransferase activity than wildtype. It only partially rescued indirect flight muscle development in rumi-mutant Drosophila. Structurally, Y57C was predicted to disrupt disulfide bonding.
quotes: 5/ II.1 | p.Y57C/ p.Y57C | 3rd | 38/F | LGMD- adult onset | 2–3 | 5 | 4 | 5 | N | Yes | >80 | No | Hyperlordosis

Notably, in vitro POGLUT1 activity assay with the normalized amounts of the WT, and the R183W and Y57C mutants of POGLUT1 proteins purified from the culture media showed much lower POGLUT1 activities compared to WT POGLUT1 (Fig. 5a).

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) identified a homozygous POGLUT1 missense variant, W308L, in a 22-year-old man with adult-onset LGMDR21 (family 6). The variant was absent from ExAC. The mutant protein was secreted poorly, which suggested destabilization, and it gave little or no rescue of Notch1 EGF1-18 secretion in POGLUT1-knockout cells.
quotes: 6/ II.4 | p.W308L/ p.W308L | 2nd | 22/M | LGMD- adult onset | 2–3 | 5 | 5 | 5 | x6 | No | 86 | No |
Thus, these results suggested that the p.I129T, p.R98W, p.C102F, and p.W308L mutations destabilized POGLUT1 proteins.

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) identified a homozygous POGLUT1 missense variant, C102F, in a 59-year-old man whose disease began in the fourth decade (family 7). The variant was predicted to disrupt a disulfide bond that stabilizes a loop involved in EGF recognition. The mutant protein was secreted poorly, did not rescue Notch1 EGF1-18 secretion, and did not rescue the muscle phenotype in rumi-mutant Drosophila.
quotes: 7/ II.1 | p.C102F/ p.C102F | 4th | 59/M | LGMD- adult onset | 2–3 | 5 | 3–4 | 5 | x3 | Yes | 85 | No |
expression of POGLUT1C102F with Mef2-GAL4 did not recue the muscle phenotype in rumi79/79 animals (Fig. 6h, i).

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) identified a homozygous POGLUT1 missense variant, R183W, in a man with infantile-onset LGMDR21 (family 9). The variant had previously been described as a Dowling-Degos disease mutation. The mutant protein was secreted normally but had markedly reduced enzymatic activity, and it only partially rescued myogenesis in Drosophila.
quotes: The homozygous missense variants p.I129T, p.R98W, p.Y57C, p.W308L, p.C102F (novel variants), and p.R183W (previously described as a DDD mutation) were identified in patients from Families 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9 respectively.
the R183W and Y57C mutants were secreted to culture media similarly to WT POGLUT1, indicating that these mutations did not destabilize POGLUT1 proteins

findings.statement: In 2 brothers with adult-onset LGMDR21 (family 8), Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) identified compound heterozygous POGLUT1 variants: a novel missense variant, Y156N, and a novel nonsense variant, c.552G>A (W184*). W184* was absent from ExAC, and Y156N was found in 2 heterozygous controls. The truncation removes the substrate-binding site. The patients' MRI pattern was typical of the disorder, which the authors took as support for pathogenicity.
quotes: In the two affected siblings from Family 8 we identified two novel variants, p.Y156N and the c.552G>A variant leading to a stop codon p.W184*.

The W184* mutation resulted in the loss of the substrate binding site, so it should be inactive (Supplementary Fig. 3b, online resource). Moreover, the muscle MRI pattern of the carrier patient was the same as in the rest of the patients, suggesting that these mutations were pathogenic as well.

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) tested patient variants in a Drosophila myogenesis rescue assay in rumi79/79 flies. Wildtype human POGLUT1 fully rescued the shortened indirect flight muscles. D233E, R183W, I129T and Y57C, which were expressed at normal levels, gave only partial rescue, and C102F gave no rescue. The authors concluded that all variants tested reduce the myogenic activity of POGLUT1.
quotes: Interestingly, the other three mutations whose expression levels were comparable with p.D233E and WT POGLUT1 (p.R183W, p.I129T and p.Y57C; Supplementary Fig. 2, online resource), also resulted in a partial rescue, with average myotubes lengths very similar to the D233E-expressing pupae (Fig. 6e, f, g, i).

We conclude that all of the mutations examined in our assay decrease the ability of human POGLUT1 to rescue the loss of fly Rumi/Poglut1 during myogenesis, even those mutations that do not affect the expression level of POGLUT1.

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) cultured primary myoblasts from the compound heterozygous D233E/R279Q patient. Compared with controls, these cells proliferated less, had fewer proliferating and self-renewing (PAX7+) cells, had more differentiating cells, and showed increased myogenin expression and fusion index. The authors concluded that slow proliferation and facilitated myogenic differentiation underlie POGLUT1-related muscular dystrophy.
quotes: The percentage of proliferating (PAX7+MyoD+) and self-renewing (PAX7+MyoD−) cells were lower in the patient than in controls, while the percentage of differentiating cells (PAX7−MyoD+) was increased in the patient (Fig. 7c-f).
Our data support the conclusion that slow proliferation and facilitated myogenic differentiation underlies POGLUT1-related muscular dystrophy.

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) proposed that LGMDR21 be considered, and POGLUT1 sequenced, in a patient with recessive LGMD who shows alpha-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation, reduced PAX7+ cells and NICD levels on muscle biopsy, and the inside-to-outside MRI pattern. They noted that the pattern must be distinguished from collagen VI myopathy, in which the outer areas of the vastus lateralis degenerate first.
quotes: Therefore, we suggest that when a patient with a recessive form of LGMD shows a combination of α-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation, reduction of PAX7+ cells and NICD levels in the muscle biopsy, and the above-mentioned muscle MRI pattern, a diagnosis of LGMD R21 should be considered and the POGLUT1 gene should be sequenced.
In COLVI mutations, the vastus lateralis muscle shows that the initial degenerative changes are most evident on the outer areas of the muscles while in POGLUT1 mutations is the opposite

findings.statement: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) found no relevant intra- or interfamilial variability in clinical features among the adult-onset patients. Across the cohort, the main source of variability was age at onset, which ranged from the first to the fifth decade. The congenital case had additional features (facial involvement, ptosis and contractures) not seen in the adult forms.
quotes: There was no relevant intra- or inter-familial variability of clinical features within the adult onset group. The most relevant variability among the whole cohort was observed in the age at onset, ranging from the 1st to the 5th decade, identifying congenital, infantile and adult onset patients.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes an ENMC workshop on reforming limb-girdle muscular dystrophy nomenclature and classification, which is relevant to the LGMDR21 / LGMD2Z naming. The title does not mention this specific disorder.

findings.statement: Straub et al. (2018) reported on the 229th ENMC international workshop, held in Naarden, the Netherlands, in March 2017, which addressed nomenclature and a reformed classification of the limb-girdle muscular dystrophies.
quotes: 229th ENMC international workshop: Limb girdle muscular dystrophies - Nomenclature and reformed classification Naarden, the Netherlands, 17-19 March 2017.

relevance_reason: The paper reports a family with autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy and a POGLUT1 variant, which is the subject of this entry. No findings are included because a safety classifier stopped the earlier attempt to extract them.
